tieuDeEn: “Hiếu” is a child's duty: our parents' kindness is like the mountains and the sea, so great that our small love can hardly repay it.

dichXuoi.en: “Hiếu” is how a child should live: be thankful to your parents. Their kindness is as great as high mountains and wide seas.

dichXuoi.en: Thinking of the high mountains and wide seas, then of our parents' kindness, we see how small our love is. How could we ever repay it?

baiHocEn: “Hiếu” is a child's duty. Our parents' kindness is as high as mountains and as wide as the sea. Be good every day to repay it.
viecTot: Tuần này, em tự làm một việc nhà mà không cần ai nhắc (gấp quần áo, quét nhà, tưới cây…) để cha mẹ vui.
en: Cô Hà welcomes you to lesson fifteen of “Lên Tám”. Last time she explained that the way to be a good person starts with “hiếu”. Today we'll look deeper at what “hiếu” means, and think about how our small love can be worthy of our parents' great kindness. Listen to today's two verses.
“Hiếu” is the duty of a child: be thankful to your parents; a father's kindness and a mother's are like the sea and the mountains.
Thinking of the mountains and the sea, then thinking of our parents' kindness – how hard it is, with a child's little love, to find anything to repay it?

The poem names our sacred duty: as children, always keep our parents' kindness in our hearts. To show how great their love is, it uses two magnificent images: a father's kindness is as firm and high as mountains; a mother's is as gentle and wide as the deep sea. Their love is the greatest protection of all.

When we think of the mountains and the sea and then of our parents, we realise how small we are. “Giả nghĩa” means to repay. How could the small love and actions of an eight-year-old ever match those mountains and seas? This question reminds us to be humble, to love our parents even more, and to try to be good every day so they can feel at peace.
